title: Lifecycle guardrails for visual primitives, tokens, and chart components
creator: Sofia Chen
description:
Purpose:
Establish a single, lightweight charter that defines contribution guardrails, RFC workflow, and a pragmatic deprecation policy for visual primitives (tokens, buttons, tables, charts). The goal is to reduce accidental regressions in product UI, make ownership clear, and provide an automated, reviewer-friendly path for engineering and design to ship safe changes to the component library.

Scope:
- Design tokens (color, spacing, typography, elevation) and token deprecation/migration patterns.
- Core components: Buttons, Inputs, Tables.
- Visualization components and primitives: Bar/Line/Pie charts, axes, legends, and chart helper utilities.
- Design tokens schema and automated publishing to packages.
- Cross-cutting: accessibility checks, theme compatibility, and telemetry for usage/regressions.

Key deliverables:
1) Contribution checklist (RI-DS contribution-checklist.md) with concrete acceptance criteria for PRs that change tokens or core visual primitives.
2) RFC template for behavior or API changes to components and tokens; lightweight approval flow (Design owner + 1 Eng reviewer + Accessibility).
3) Deprecation playbook with stages: Notice -> Soft deprecation (flag + compatibility shim) -> Removal (major version) and suggested migration codemods.
4) CI guard rails: token-lint, visual-diff, accessibility audit, and bundle-size alert.
5) Metrics dashboard: percent usage of variant tokens, number of components referencing deprecated tokens, regressions post-release.

Proposed contribution workflow:
- Small cosmetic token edits (non-API affecting token rename/space) can be merged with 1 designer + 1 engineer approval if visual diff passes and token-lint is green.
- Any change that alters component API, variant behavior, or chart rendering must go through an RFC (short-form: 1 page) with a 3-business-day comment window. RFC reviewers: design lead, platform engineer, visualization library owner, accessibility engineer.
- For charting changes that affect data representation (aggregation, axes defaults), require a staging rollout with a canary tag and telemetry for top-10 customers.

Deprecation policy (practical summary):
- Stage 0: Announcement — add deprecation note in CHANGELOG and design system site; maintainers tag impacted packages. Window: immediate.
- Stage 1: Soft-deprecate — introduce a compatibility shim and log warnings in dev console. Mark 'deprecated' in docs. Window: minimum 3 releases / 90 days.
- Stage 2: Removal candidate — create a removal PR that upgrades package major version and includes migration codemod or script. Communicate via release notes, Slack #platform-alerts, and email to opt-in consumers. Window: target next major release after 90+ days.

Migration support:
- Provide codemods (jscodeshift) and sample recipes for common token renames and chart option migrations.
- Add an incremental migration mode to design-token transformer to emit both old and new tokens during a transitional release.

Automation and CI requirements:
- token-lint: validates token names, tokens referenced by components, and semantic usage (color-on-background contrast).
- visual-diff: Percy/Chromatic snapshots with thresholded tolerances by component.
- accessibility: axe checks in storybook snapshots and automated keyboard navigation smoke tests for interactive components.
- telemetry: instrumentation hooks to count usage of component props and token keys (opt-in, privacy-preserving).

Ownership and reviews:
- Each component and token group must list an owner on docs (team + primary contact).
- Pull requests touching tokens or visualization primitives should list the owner in PR description and ping them.
- Final approval matrix: Design Owner (visual/UX intent), Eng Owner (API/implementation), Accessibility (a11y).

Rollout plan:
- Publish charter to the design system site and Confluence (link below).
- Pilot with token changes for spacing scale and a chart axis config change in a staging release.
- Iterate on checklist and add codemods based on pilot feedback.

Open questions / trade-offs:
- Strictness vs. speed: balancing slower RFC cadence vs. developer velocity. Proposed compromise: short-form RFCs for minor breaking changes (<2 components impacted).
- Telemetry opt-in: legal/privacy approval required for telemetry. Will coordinate with Security & Legal.
- Deprecation window length: 90 days recommended; may be extended for high-impact surface areas.

References and links:
- Draft RFC template: https://confluence.redwood/DS/rfc-template-v2 (internal)
- Prototype codemod repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/design-codemods/pull/6
- Visual test harness stories: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/visual-harness-stories (internal)
- Example PR implementing soft-deprecation for color tokens: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ui/pull/824
